title: Ines and the Thorn
premise: Marguerite Thornbury, a mercenary bound to the silent god Veyra, takes a dying courier's map and learns it charts a buried vault where the god's stolen voice has been hidden for two centuries. Pursued by the Ashen Order, zealots who silenced Veyra to seize divine power, Marguerite descends the smuggler roads of Thornfell with a fugitive scholar, Tam, who knows how the voice can be restored — or weaponized. Betrayals strip away her crew, her faith, and her certainty that returning the voice will bring justice rather than catastrophe. In the vault, Marguerite must choose: give the god its voice back and risk a holy war, or destroy it forever, severing herself from every oath she has ever sworn. She shatters the voice, freeing the mountains from divine manipulation, and walks out of Thornfell owing nothing to any god but carrying the memory of everyone the silence cost.
about_author: Elodie Oyelaran is a former trail guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through mountain passes that appear, thinly disguised, throughout her fiction. She writes fantasy about oaths, debts, and the people who survive both, and lives in a stone farmhouse with too many maps and one opinionated goat.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She guides a caravan through the Thornfell passes, praying to Veyra out of habit though the god has been silent for years. A routine job, a paid debt, an empty altar. The beat establishes her competence, her cynicism, and the hollow ritual of faith without answer.

chapters.title: The Courier's Last Mile
chapters.summary: A wounded stranger stumbles into her camp at dusk, pursued by riders in ash-grey cloaks. He presses a leather map into her hands and dies whispering 'the voice below the stone.' The Order arrives minutes later. Marguerite lies to their faces. The beat is terror and the first pull of a debt she never asked to owe.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Marguerite tries to sell the map in the border town of Greymill and discovers the buyer she approaches is found dead by morning. She realizes possession alone is a death sentence. The beat is dawning claustrophobia: there is no version of this where she simply walks away.

chapters.title: Tam of the Sealed Library
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. A scholar of the sealed archives recognizes the map's markings and burns his own research before fleeing the city. He is caught by Order agents but escapes with the help of an old debt. The beat introduces the second protagonist and the scale of the conspiracy hunting them.

chapters.title: An Unwilling Partnership
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Tam collide in Greymill's underbelly, each believing the other is bait. After a knife's-edge standoff, Tam explains the map: it leads to Veyra's stolen voice, hidden when the Order silenced the god. Marguerite refuses to believe it. The beat is reluctant alliance built on mutual distrust.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: They take the hidden paths only Marguerite knows, evading Order checkpoints. Tam's city softness nearly kills them both; Marguerite's ruthlessness unsettles him. In a cave shrine, Marguerite prays again and, for the first time, feels something answer — or imagines she does. The beat is grudging respect and flickering hope.

chapters.title: The Ashen Vigil
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Serane's POV. She interrogates the Greymill buyer's associates and reconstructs the courier's route. Flashbacks reveal the Order's founding sin: they did not silence a mad god, they muzzled a truthful one. The beat reframes the antagonist as a true believer guarding a lie.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: At the river crossing, the ferrywoman demands payment Marguerite cannot make and offers instead to take Tam's memories as toll — a glimpse of what the Order's old magic can do. They flee upstream instead. The beat shows the price of survival made literal and foreshadows the book's central trade.

chapters.title: Ghosts of the Company
chapters.summary: Marguerite's old mercenary company, the Thornbury Blades, catches up with her — hired by the Order to retrieve the map. Her former captain, Doss, offers her a way out: give up the map, keep her life. She refuses and fights her way clear, wounding a friend. The beat is grief and the severing of her last safe harbor.

chapters.title: What Tam Remembered
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. He confesses his family helped the Order seal the vault two centuries ago; the map was his grandmother's, and his research was a penance. Marguerite's fury nearly ends the partnership. The beat is betrayal, then the harder truth: they are both carrying inherited sins.

chapters.title: The Pass of Hanged Men
chapters.summary: A winter storm traps them in a pass littered with Order gallows from the old purges. Ambushed by Blades and Order agents simultaneously, they survive only through Marguerite's brutal knowledge of the terrain. Tam saves her life; the ledger between them begins to balance. The beat is hard-won trust forged in violence.

chapters.title: The God That Answers
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a ruined temple, Marguerite dreams of Veyra for the first time — fragments of the god's voice leaking through the seal, showing her the war the Order fears and the peace the silence bought. She wakes weeping and cannot say whether it was a message or a trap. The beat is vertigo: the truth may be worse than the lie.

chapters.title: Serane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. She corners Tam alone and offers him absolution — his family's name restored — if he delivers Marguerite and the map. Tam neither accepts nor refuses, and Serane lets him go, certain he will break. The beat deepens Serane's intelligence and plants the seed of the third-act betrayal.

chapters.title: The Underroad
chapters.summary: They descend into the Underroad, the smugglers' artery beneath Thornfell, guided by Marguerite's memory of a route she swore never to take again — the one where her brother died. The dark strips away her armor; she tells Tam the truth of her oath to Veyra, sworn over his body. The beat is the emotional floor of the book.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember
chapters.summary: The vault's antechambers test intruders with constructed memories: Tam relives his family's sealing of the god, Marguerite relives her brother's death, each forced to watch without intervening. They pass only by accepting what they did. The beat is the theme made mechanical — memory as toll, survival as debt.

chapters.title: The Voice Below the Stone
chapters.summary: They reach the vault and find Veyra's voice: a living resonance caged in stone, half-mad from two centuries of silence, screaming truths the Order buried. It offers Marguerite everything — her brother back, her god restored — if she frees it. The beat is temptation at full power.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Oaths
chapters.summary: Serane and the Order breach the vault, with Doss and the Blades in tow. Tam, cornered by Serane's earlier bargain, hesitates — and in that hesitation Doss is killed by Order crossfire meant for Marguerite. The battle for the vault begins. The beat is catastrophe: every debt comes due at once.

chapters.title: Truth as a Weapon
chapters.summary: The voice, half-freed, floods the vault with raw truth — Serane sees the Order's founding massacre, the Blades see who hired them, Tam sees his family's crime in full. Zealots kneel or shatter. Serane, unmade by what she learns, turns her blade on her own Grand Inquisitor. The beat is the climax: justice outside the law, delivered by truth itself.

chapters.title: The Choice of Marguerite Thornbury
chapters.summary: The voice, freed but broken, begs Marguerite to carry it into the world — to make every mortal hear what it knows. She understands it would ignite the war the Order feared, truth wielded as a weapon that spares no one. She chooses silence: not the Order's muzzle, but a willing ending. The beat is the book's moral summit.

chapters.title: What the Silence Buys
chapters.summary: Marguerite releases the voice into the mountain rather than the world; the vault collapses, the resonance dissolving into stone and snow. Tam chooses to stay behind to record what happened, his penance accepted at last. Marguerite carries him out against his protests. The beat is sacrifice, grief, and the cost made visible.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Down
chapters.summary: Marguerite descends Thornfell alone, oathless for the first time in her life. She passes the ferrywoman and pays her toll willingly — a single memory of the voice's song, kept so she never forgets what she gave up. The beat is quiet reckoning: survival paid in full, and worth it.

chapters.title: Ines and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Epilogue. In Greymill, an orphan girl named Ines hears the mountain hum on the wind and asks Marguerite, now a road-warden, what it says. 'Nothing,' Marguerite says. 'That's how you know it's at peace.' The beat is resolution: justice without a god, memory without a master, and a road still worth walking.
